clue.text: Put thoughts into words — and fast!

definitions.meaning: to voice or state an idea
an ... train or delivery is a fast one

explanation.surface: An urging to speak your mind, and quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an idea is to express it, and an express service is a speedy one.

clue.text: Executive sat out in the open

parts.note: EX is a dictionary abbreviation for executive
to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat gives posed

explanation.surface: A company boss is seated outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left uncovered, with no shelter, is laid bare to view.

clue.text: Mediaeval country game in a new guise

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: the letters of the words in and a appear in a new form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A medieval land's sport has been revived in a fresh form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new guise' rearranges IN A into NIA after POLO. Polonia is the medieval Latin name for Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Polonia is the Latin name used in medieval documents for Poland.

clue.text: People may well pass out here!

definitions.text: People may well pass out here!

parts.words: People may well pass out here!
parts.note: pass out suggests fainting, but here it means simply going out through a doorway

explanation.surface: A spot where people tend to faint.
explanation.definitionFit: Doorways marked for leaving a building are where crowds go out.

clue.text: Father Christmas will hold nothing, nothing, up. It's a bloomer

indicators.note: Santa will hold, i.e. contain, the other pieces inside him

parts.note: Santa is Father Christmas

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: nil means nothing
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Santa holding up a couple of zeros turns out to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NIL + O into OLIN, which 'will hold' puts inside SANTA. 'Bloomer' is meant to read as a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Santolina, cotton lavender, is a shrub grown for its flowers, so it blooms.

clue.text: Reliable supporters when things get rough

definitions.text: Reliable supporters when things get rough

parts.words: Reliable supporters when things get rough
parts.note: supporters suggests loyal friends, but here they are a sailor's legs that stay steady on a rolling deck

explanation.surface: Praise for friends who stand by you in hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor who has found balance on a pitching ship walks steadily in heavy weather.

clue.text: The decline of the team accepting money

indicators.note: the team takes in, i.e. accepts, the money

parts.note: a side is a team
L stands for pound (libra), a unit of money

explanation.surface: A football club's slump after taking cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall in value or standards is a downward drop.

clue.text: Topical — so unexpected of an old preacher

indicators.note: the letters come out in an unexpected order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a topical sermon was surprising for a preacher of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostolic means relating to the apostles, the early Christian preachers.

clue.text: Not a good-looker!

parts.note: a good-looker is usually an attractive person, but read literally it is a kindly gaze; this gaze is a malicious one

explanation.surface: An unkind verdict on someone's appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A malign glance believed to bring harm is the opposite of a benign gaze.

clue.text: Detectives involved in party division

indicators.note: the detectives are wrapped up in, i.e. inside, the party

parts.note: a set is a social group or party
G-men are US federal detectives (FBI agents)

explanation.surface: Police officers mixed up with a faction of a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one section or portion of a whole.

clue.text: Religious gripping cross on back seat

indicators.note: the first piece grips, i.e. holds inside it, the second

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, religious
ill, as in ill-humoured, can mean cross or bad-tempered
taken as written

explanation.surface: A believer clutching a crucifix in the rear seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' puts ILL inside PI to make PILLI. PI is old slang for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillion is a passenger seat behind the rider on a motorbike.

clue.text: Evening work

parts.note: evening suggests the hours after dusk, but here it means making flat and smooth, as with creased clothes

explanation.surface: A night shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes with a hot iron smooths out the creases.

clue.text: Among the best of building materials, one stands out

definitions.text: Among the best of building materials

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: One type of stone stands out among quality building materials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ONESTANDS. The clue's 'one stands out' reads as praise, which disguises the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock long valued for construction.

clue.text: A topic for discussion in depth: emergency arrangements

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Discussing emergency plans in depth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run across 'depTH EMErgency'.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject chosen for a talk or essay is its central idea.

clue.text: Many a would-be Casanova gets the bird!

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, so many
a rake is a womaniser, an aspiring Casanova

explanation.surface: A ladies' man is given the brush-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' sounds like being booed off; here 'the bird' is the definition. Casanova was a famous Italian seducer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, a waterfowl.

clue.text: Have in mind to go in without a word of thanks

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the first piece sits outside the second

parts.note: to enter in is to go in
ta is an informal British word for thanks

explanation.surface: Barging in without saying thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so ENTER IN wraps TA. TA is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain an idea is to consider it or hold it in thought.

clue.text: On the rocks taking in sun and air

parts.note: taken as written
Sol is the Latin name for the sun
to vent a grievance is to air it

explanation.surface: A drink on ice outdoors in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' suggests a drink served with ice; here it means bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: A business on the rocks is bankrupt, unable to pay its debts.

clue.text: Dior's bed, a fantastic piece of furniture

indicators.note: fantastic suggests the letters are reworked in a wild new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of Dior's, its S included

explanation.surface: A designer's bed described as a wonderful piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges DIORSBEDA. Dior is a French fashion house.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard is a long cabinet in a dining room for storing dishes.

clue.text: A knave possibly — or curt cad anyway

indicators.note: anyway suggests the letters set out in any order you like

explanation.surface: A scoundrel, or a rude cad, whatever you call him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' rearranges ORCURTCAD. 'Knave' looks like a rogue, matching 'cad', but the definition is the playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave (jack), queen and king are the picture cards in a pack.

clue.text: She finds acclaim in foreign secret service

indicators.note: the praise goes in the agency's letters

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, foreign to a British setter
to laud is to praise or acclaim

explanation.surface: A woman wins praise from an overseas spy agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudia is a girl's name, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Having no title can appear mundane

indicators.note: the letters can appear in another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being without a title can look ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nameless or anonymous carries no name or heading.

clue.text: Cold girl, but kind

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl who seems chilly is actually kind-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a category or sort of thing.

clue.text: Tot on heath getting confused

parts.note: to tot up is to add
ling is heather, the plant of heathland

explanation.surface: A toddler wandering on a moor and losing the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Addling means muddling or becoming muddled.

clue.text: Rose must present second petition

parts.note: a prayer is a petition or request

explanation.surface: A flower offers another plea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like the flower or the verb; it is the perforated nozzle of a watering can.
explanation.definitionFit: A watering can's rose is a nozzle that delivers water as a spray.

clue.text: Little American sailor bearing right

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
NE, north-east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A small American seaman heading to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: Li'l Abner is the hillbilly hero of a long-running American comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Li'l Abner is a US comic-strip character, so he is the little American.

clue.text: Get the needle and dress up

definitions.meaning: to take up a needle and sew decorative stitching
to embellish a story with invented details

explanation.surface: Getting annoyed and then putting on fancy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the needle' usually means become irritated; here it means work with a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative needlework and exaggerating a tale both mean adding ornament.

clue.text: Directions to prosecute follow

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions
to sue is to take legal action against someone

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to bring a court case come next.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to happen afterwards as a result.

clue.text: Sheepish individual coming round about six

indicators.note: the individual comes round about, i.e. encircles, the next piece

parts.note: one means a single individual
VI is the Roman numeral six

explanation.surface: A bashful person comes to about six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' looks like embarrassed but means relating to sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means of or like sheep, from Latin ovis.

clue.text: Deem equivocal answer given is humiliating

indicators.note: equivocal means uncertain, so the letters are not settled and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Thinking a vague reply is degrading.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, degrading them.

clue.text: State shortly in a built-up area there'll be some rancour

indicators.note: the state goes in the other letters

parts.note: a city is a large built-up area
ID is the postal abbreviation of Idaho, a US state

explanation.surface: Bitterness will come with a state in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidity of manner is sourness or bitterness, much like resentment.

clue.text: An old writer, so somewhat slow

parts.note: Dante was a medieval Italian poet

explanation.surface: An ancient author, rather slow.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical direction for a moderately slow tempo.

clue.text: This makes a profound difference to the port

definitions.text: This makes a profound difference to the port

parts.words: This makes a profound difference to the port
parts.note: profound suggests important, but here it means deep: the vessel deepens a harbour by scooping silt

explanation.surface: Something that transforms a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that scoops mud from a harbour bed keeps channels deep for shipping.
